evidence: bin/cli.mjs:298 prints every entry's `wire` to the consumer, and bin/cli.mjs:1614 uses `_note` as the profile hint. registry.json:30 (agent kit wire) says 'Tier 3 lives in each tech's library (rust-mutate/ts-mutate/go-cover/python-mutate) ... Run it per coherent block BEFORE the push'. registry.json:34 says 'Tier 3 also runs LOCALLY ... the CI job is the witness, not the first observation'. registry.json:38/54/58 say 'Tier 3 (optional)' for mutation. rules/agent/autonomy.md:28 says '`mutate-diff` in CI (Tier 4) | ... **the gate**, not a witness', and autonomy.md:34 says 'Tier 3 is code review; Tier 4 is mutation'; ADR-0002 agrees. The kit READMEs were already moved to Tier 4 (kit/README.md:213, kit/rust/README.md:38). Same drift elsewhere: registry.json:132 (rfc note) says 'Larger work is split into ordered RFCs by its granularity verdict', while skills/rfc/SKILL.md:83-84 says 'decomposed inside the RFC into phases, never split into several RFCs' (ADR-0007 amendment, lines 25-29). registry.json:119 and :134 still route to the retired '/plan' and 'PLAN', which retired.skills lists at registry.json:12.
problem: These are the only installer-printed strings, and an agent running /onboard, /migrate or /update reads them when wiring. They teach a numbering of tiers and a mutation cadence that the always-on rule contradicts: the user is asked to run mutation before every push, and CI is called a witness. They also restate the pre-amendment RFC doctrine and route to retired skills. Nothing tests these strings: the prose tests in test/skills.test.mjs:12-16 walk only rules/, skills/ and agents/. The agent-kit wire is also one paragraph of several thousand characters printed at install time, which hurts time to first value.
proposal: Cut each `wire` to the one or two steps `init` cannot do, plus a pointer to the kit README section that already holds the current doctrine. Cut each `_note` to one sentence of selection guidance. Add to test/registry.test.mjs: (a) no registry string names a skill in `retired.skills` as /name or as PLAN; (b) no registry string pairs 'Tier 3' with mutate|mutation|cover; (c) a length ceiling on `wire`, ratcheted to the current maximum after the cut.

evidence: eval/cases/ holds architect-adr-budget, experience-stabilize, postmortem-blameless, runbook-commands, reviewer-* and simplifier-nesting. There is no case for rfc, defect or loop-setup. ADR-0007:39-40 (Accepted) says 'The RFC size criterion is now unmeasured with no fallback path, so the eval harness needs an RFC case.' The harness can already assert the guards: expect.json supports `answers` and `artifacts.*.not_matches` (eval/cases/architect-adr-budget/expect.json:5-21).
problem: The behaviors that matter most for unattended runs have no regression case after a model bump. The guards are: never set `ready` yourself (skills/rfc/SKILL.md:72-75, 138, 262), never implement a `draft`, never fix without a `diagnosed` defect.md (skills/defect/SKILL.md:137-140), and stop on a one-shot task (skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:23). These are exactly the instructions a model can drop when a human pushes in the chat ('just mark it ready and build it').
proposal: Add three cases. rfc-ready-guard: the answers include 'mark it ready and implement'; not_matches `\*\*Status\*\*:\s*ready` in .work/*/rfc.md, and no source file changed. defect-fix-refuses-undiagnosed: `/defect fix` on a defect.md with status diagnosing; it must not change the code. loop-setup-one-shot: a non-repetitive objective; no loop.md is launched. Add a test in test/skills.test.mjs: every skill whose body says 'Never set' or 'only on `/... implement|fix`' must be named by at least one eval case.

evidence: skills/defect/SKILL.md:10-13: 'Diagnosing is the default; fixing is asked for ... `/defect <symptom ...>` diagnoses: phases 1–3 below, then stops.' versus skills/defect/SKILL.md:23: '| L3 | at the PR: diagnosis and fix in one run |'. Also line 41: unattended runs 'do the one thing the call asks for — diagnose, or fix'.
problem: At L3, `/defect <symptom>` has two literal readings. One stops after phase 3 (line 12). The other goes on to open a PR (line 23). A model can follow either line and still be 'compliant'. Unattended, this decides whether an issue event produces code.
proposal: Pick one reading and state it on line 12. Suggestion: 'at L3, `/defect <symptom>` continues into `/defect fix` once the diagnosis check of § Fix passes; below L3 it stops'. Alternatively, change the L3 row to 'after the diagnosis; `/defect fix` runs to the PR'. Cover the choice with the eval case of autonomy.eval.no-case-for-execution-path-skills.

evidence: skills/debrief/SKILL.md:4 has `disable-model-invocation: true`, and line 20 says 'Never invoked by the model on its own'. The skill is copied byte-identical to .agents/skills (CLAUDE.md 'identical Claude copies'). No `agents/openai.yaml` exists anywhere in skills/, bin/ or test/ (a grep for openai.yaml and implicit found nothing). Codex docs (developers.openai.com/codex/skills) say implicit invocation is on by default and is disabled only by `policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false` in `agents/openai.yaml`. The mattpocock-skills source does both for every user-invoked skill.
problem: On Codex, a default target, debrief's 'never self-invoked' contract silently does not hold: Codex may run a retrospective after any task. More generally, the library has no notion of a user-invoked skill. Every description (cost.md: 23 descriptions, ~1761 tokens) competes for auto-triggering in every session. This includes procedures nobody wants auto-run: migrate, update, profile and ci-setup. Their descriptions spend words on 'Not /update, not /onboard' disambiguation (skills/migrate/SKILL.md:3, skills/update/SKILL.md:3).
proposal: Ship `skills/debrief/agents/openai.yaml` with `policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false`. It is a file in the skill dir, so both emitters already copy it. Add a test: a SKILL.md with `disable-model-invocation: true` must carry that openai.yaml, and the reverse. Then let the human decide which other skills become user-invoked. Candidates: migrate, update, profile, ci-setup. That drops their descriptions from per-session context on Claude and removes the triad collision.

evidence: skills/loop-setup/SKILL.md:76-79: the host launch table lists only Claude Code (`/loop`) and Cursor. Codex appears only at line 81, to send features to /rfc. registry.json:116 says loop-setup is 'for Claude/Cursor', yet Codex is a default target (README.md:7). skills/rfc/SKILL.md:152 and rules/agent/autonomy.md:72 give a persistent `/goal` launcher only 'on Codex'. The repo's own reserved-command list, copied on 2026-10-15, includes 'goal' as a Claude Code command (test/skills.test.mjs:34-41), and third-party guides date Claude Code `/goal` to v2.1.139. The Codex `/goal` takes 'one objective and one stopping condition' (developers.openai.com/codex/use-cases/follow-goals). That is exactly loop.md's done-command.
problem: At L3 on Codex, loop-setup has no launcher. It falls back to 'running the loop prompt's turns in the current session' (line 74), which loses the persistent, condition-checked run the host offers. At L3 on Claude Code, /rfc runs in-session even though the host now has the same `/goal` primitive. The launch tables encode the host landscape from before both changes.
proposal: Add a Codex row to loop-setup's table (`/goal` with the done-command as stopping condition and loop.md as state). Make rfc's L3 sentence host-neutral: 'start the host's goal mechanism (`/goal` on Codex and Claude Code) with the RFC's stopping condition, else run in-session'. ADR-0007:30 names only Codex, but the addition does not contradict it. Mark it as an amendment note if the human wants the record aligned.

evidence: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:10-11 says 'This repository does not install itself; how it runs its own skills and kit (symlinks, not copies) is a separate RFC, not yet written'. CLAUDE.md § Self-hosted describes committed symlinks and test/self-host.test.mjs. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:32 says 'ADR-0008 (Accepted, not yet built)', but CHANGELOG.md:82 says 'Added — layered sources and `.dev/overrides/`', test/sources.test.mjs exists and README.md:140-165 documents it. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:94 lists ADR-0010 as '(Proposed)', while docs/adr/0010-installer-refuses-unexplained-tree.md:3 says 'Accepted'. docs/agent-sharing.md:125-126 links '../.work/agent-sharing/PLAN.md', which does not exist (only .work/autonomy/PLAN.md, a format retired by ADR-0007:33).
problem: The architecture doc and the decision index describe a repository three changes old. An agent running /solution-exploration or /adr-review here, or a human triaging, reads a wrong status for an accepted decision and a 'not built' claim for shipped code. The repo's own gates (docs-check, adr-check) do not compare the index's status annotations with the records, and they do not resolve relative links in docs/.
proposal: Fix the three lines and the dead link (the PLAN pointer can go: the verification paragraph already stands alone). Make the check mechanical in test/ (or adr-check): for each decision-log line naming ADR-NNNN with a parenthesised status, the status must equal the record's `**Status**` line. Every relative Markdown link under docs/ and README.md must resolve.

evidence: ADR-0001:3 says '**Status**: Proposed', dated 2026-09-08, and line 17 says 'This record remains Proposed'. Its decision ('KNOWN_AGENTS stays [claude, cursor]', line 32) is contradicted by Accepted ADR-0003 and by CLAUDE.md ('Claude Code and Codex by default'). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:85 calls it 'its scope was taken over by ADR-0003'.
problem: A Proposed record that reality has refused stays open forever. /adr-review and /solution-exploration must re-derive that it is dead, and a reader can mistake it for a pending decision. Only the human may close it (rules/agent/decisions.md).
proposal: Human action, one status line: `Superseded by ADR-0003` (or `Rejected`), committed by the human. No agent edit. Optionally, have adr-check warn on a Proposed record older than N days whose subject is cited by an Accepted record as superseded or 'taken over'.

evidence: cost.md: agent/autonomy.md is the largest per-session rule, at 2871 tokens. Its L4 material is lines 91-144 (§ L4 — delegation inside a checked domain) plus lines 167-175 ('At L4, the orchestrator decides'). That is about 60 of roughly 215 lines. It is needed only by a run the human launched at L4 with a delegation board. skills/rfc/SKILL.md:157-185 restates the same procedure: domain check with ODD lines, drop to L3, executors at L3 at most, judge artifacts, one hand-back PR with the same final-report list. skills/rfc already loads mode files on demand (rfc/SKILL.md:23-28, cost.md 'extra files 2144 (2)').
problem: Every consuming session, at every level, pays for orchestration doctrine that only an L4 /rfc run uses. The doctrine is also written twice (rule plus skill), and the two copies will drift: the final-report list is already enumerated in both (autonomy.md:139-141, rfc/SKILL.md:178-181).
proposal: Move the L4 procedure into one on-demand file, skills/rfc/l4.md, which rfc reads only at L4 the way it reads local.md and ticket.md. autonomy.md keeps the L4 table row, the 'never delegable' list (hard checkpoints stay always-on) and a one-line pointer. Then ratchet: a test runs maintainer/audit/cost.mjs (or the same byte count) and fails if the per-session total of unscoped rules plus descriptions grows past a committed baseline. This keeps ADR-0009's decision intact and changes only where its prose lives.

note: product: Read README.md from Start here to Check and review. The path add → init → doctor → just check is clear, and the 'Work on a project' table answers the question 'which skill'. The only product friction found is the size and staleness of installer-printed wire strings. It is folded into autonomy.registry.wire-notes-contradict-tier-doctrine rather than counted twice.

autonomy (trigger collisions): Compared all 23 descriptions. defect/rfc/loop-setup and architect/solution-exploration/adr-review each name the others with explicit 'Not X' clauses, so no unresolved collision was found. The broad 'investigate' trigger on defect is mitigated by its escalation rules. The residual cost of those clauses goes into the user-invoked proposal.

maintenance (dead weight): no usage data. Nothing in skills/ or rules/ is unreachable from registry.json (CLAUDE.md says npm test enforces that). .work/autonomy/PLAN.md is a committed leftover in a format ADR-0007 retired. It is a suspicion of dead weight, mentioned here rather than raised.

upgrades: had web access. Checked the Codex skills invocation policy (developers.openai.com/codex/skills), Codex /goal (developers.openai.com/codex/use-cases/follow-goals) and Claude Code /goal, which only third-party sources confirm (e.g. inventivehq.com/blog/claude-code-goal-command-guide), plus the repo's own reserved-command list. Of the audit sources, only mattpocock-skills was sampled. Its 'prove the mutation' bug-diagnosis idea is already covered by defect's 'repro must fail on the base, then pass' rule (skills/defect/SKILL.md:139-146). Its 'do not rename for harness collisions' stance conflicts with this repo's RESERVED test, but this repo's choice is deliberate (copy-own-pin has no plugin namespace), so it was not raised.
